findings.summary: The collector/reducer has no concrete #90 exact-store or coherent paged-volume composition.
findings.evidence: #69 design.md:37-56 collects only GetVolume and derives holdings/redundancy/availability from legacy node membership. At mapped #90 contracts.md:12-28,47-55,65-88, ACTIVE Volume/ChunkMeta identity_schema=2 omit the legacy membership/move fields, expose exact ReplicaRef(node,device_uuid) and Node store_uuid/store_generation, and forbid fallback. An alive node with replacement B does not make its earned A ref available. core-design.md:61-73 also makes initial_pending_refs a planned rather than earned initial ISR, with a chunk-wide initial-I/O barrier; counting len(ISR) alone would label that initialization healthy. #90 budgets.md:45-81,106-110 retains legal paged_legacy volumes for which ordinary GetVolume explicitly refuses and defines ReadIdentityVolumePage with pinned incarnation/header/gate/mode predicates. #69's Client/Reader contract has no adapter/hook. #91 reader-contract.md:233-260 already owns the shared page allowlist extension, so this is a missing local consumer composition, not a request to reopen #91.
findings.fix: Add a proposed whoever-lands-second #69/#90 consumer adapter referencing #90's identity-v4 and #91's sole Reader page-auth owner. Define installed-schema/profile validation, exact incarnation and canonical refs, separate committed/planned/earned counts, pending-initial blocked hints, and current UUID/G-aware availability without converting registration into membership. Define coherent full/paged acquisition with exact initial/discovered and later pinned predicates, contiguous indices, final completion, no mixed attempts and existing aggregate/time/RPC limits; reject unsupported/invalid views explicitly. Add future fixtures with empty legacy projections, alive B/earned A, original-A return with new G, pending initial copies, full/paged equivalence, FE0/LID, predicate churn/missing/duplicate pages and late failure. Do not copy guard admission eligibility or its stricter NotFound policy.

findings.summary: The tombstone collection contract is incompatible with #90 and can erase distinct cleanup observations.
findings.evidence: #69 design.md:39-40,67-68,87-89 calls node-only ListTombstones once per registered node and deduplicates by volume while preserving full Nodes/Pending sets. Current service.go:584-614 and meta.proto:169-184 implement that legacy shape. Mapped #90 contracts.md:95-163 instead requires an exact ref, explicit limit/cursor, current G for own-node IO or G=0 for administrator inspection, returns <=32 per-ref summaries and complete/next_cursor, omits legacy Nodes/Pending, and refuses node-only requests in ACTIVE. The list rule names IO/admin, not the new Reader. One registered node may have old-A and new-B pending refs and same-name volume reuse must be distinguished by first_epoch/LID/deletion_operation. A current UUID-only scan would hide the unplugged A tombstone, and volume-only dedup collapses distinct ref/incarnation observations. #91's shared extension adds only ReadIdentityVolumePage, not this tombstone inspection adapter.
findings.fix: Specify a concrete bounded read-only ListTombstones inspection composition for Readers that preserves the approved node-scoped administrative read intent, including how registered-node enumeration reaches retained historical UUID refs. For example, define a distinct read-only node-prefix inspection request/cursor over #90's existing node/uuid index, with fixed examined-key/page/byte limits and caller/node-scoped cursor validation; it grants no confirmation or current-store possession authority. Consume all bounded pages including empty nonfinal pages, reject repeated/nonprogress cursors and budget overflow, and key retained rows by volume+incarnation+deletion_operation+exact ref. State observed coverage and unknown totals precisely rather than reconstructing omitted full Nodes/Pending as complete; preserve a separately validated legacy adapter. Add actual-service future fixtures for Reader permission, old/new UUIDs on one registered node, >32 rows, skipped/empty pages, churn/name reuse and no successful partial view.

findings.summary: Bare ListVolumes can report a damaged cluster as an empty successful observation.
findings.evidence: #69 spec.md invariant/S5 forbids failed/incomplete observation becoming healthy empty; design.md:37-42 uses ordinary ListVolumes without a completeness contract. Actual meta/service/service.go:845-857 silently skips malformed header JSON, so a sole damaged published header gives success with zero IDs and no GetVolume to fail. #77 only fixes coherent named reads. The already-clear shared #91 reader-contract.md:7-70 owns additive require_complete/complete, bounded validation of every candidate header, and explicit old-server incompatibility; #69 does not consume it.
findings.fix: Add the local whoever-lands-second #69/#91 strict-list consumer hook, sending require_complete=true and requiring complete=true before a successful status view. Reference #91 as the single service-contract owner; do not fork/edit/reopen it. Treat old-server default false, malformed/contradictory headers or strict-list errors as visible command failure with empty stdout. Keep #69's allowed bounded NotFound omissions and snapshot:false: no guard-style bracketing, candidate history or eviction eligibility is required. Future actual-service-to-status fixtures must cover sole bad header, mixed good/bad, valid Creating/Deleting omission, old server false and a valid empty cluster.

findings.summary: Shared health and nested schema are still underspecified for mixed unknown and omitted observations.
findings.evidence: #69 intent.md What we want 2 asks for one definition of chunk/volume/node states; spec.md:S3 and design.md:51-56 only say compare ISR/RF and observed alive/minISR, mark unknown nodes, and count holdings/targets. The version1 output fixes only top-level names at design.md:66-74, with no nested state/count fields or chunk-to-volume reduction. For RF3/min2, one alive+one dead+one unknown and two alive+one unknown need different hints; 'unknown nodes explicitly' does not decide either. A listed volume omitted as NotFound also makes node holdings/target totals observational lower bounds, yet the plan has no completeness/denominator rule for these derived counts. #71 spec.md:50-56 and contracts.md:248-261 reuse #69 under-replicated chunk/volume counts, so that consumer needs a stable local contract rather than independently inventing reduction.
findings.fix: Define the nested version1 View fields and exact pure reductions once: validated RF/min/geometry/set/move inputs; committed redundancy per chunk; explicit earned/initial distinctions under R1-C1; availability with known-alive/known-dead/unknown counts and threshold rules; deterministic per-volume aggregation; node holdings/served-volume counts and their observation coverage. Preserve an omitted volume as an identified allowed omission, and mark totals that exclude it as incomplete/observed rather than complete zero. Reference #71's existing under-replicated metric meaning without importing telemetry, CRDs or a dashboard. Add table-driven fixtures for both threshold examples, mixed chunk states, unknown target, all/no omissions, and stable JSON/human equivalence.
